sections.html:
St. Johns has three offices that matter for a property owner. One sets values, one bills and collects, and one keeps the deed records. Each sits at 75 West Cleveland and opens Monday through Thursday, 6:30 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. Friday is closed.

OfficeRolePhoneMailing box
AssessorValues real and personal property, handles first-level appeals928-337-7624PO Box 770
TreasurerMails tax notices, collects tax, runs the tax lien sale928-337-7629PO Box 699
RecorderRecords and indexes deeds and other documents928-337-7515PO Box 425

Schools and special districts receive their share of the revenue from the Treasurer, based on their mill levies. To see rates broken out by district, call the Assessor's office.

Two installments make up the yearly bill, one on October 1 and one on March 1. A.R.S. 42-18052 makes the October half late once 5:00 p.m. passes on November 1, and the March half late once 5:00 p.m. passes on May 1.

  • A bill of $100 or less for the year is paid whole on October 1 and goes delinquent when 5:00 p.m. passes on December 31.
  • A delinquency date on a weekend or holiday slides to 5:00 p.m. the next business day.
  • Interest on delinquent accounts runs at 16% a year, prorated monthly.
  • Notices go out by mail even when a lender pays through escrow, and a notice that never arrives is no excuse for paying late.

With two installments, a seller who closes between October and March may have one half paid and the other open. Open the Treasurer's account search and look at both halves before you pick a closing date.

Payment options are mail, a card online, or the Treasurer's counter in St. Johns. The county prefers mailed payments, with checks written to the Apache County Treasurer.

  • With a payment coupon, mail to Apache County Treasurer, PO Box 4262, Houston, TX 77210.
  • Without a coupon, mail to Apache County Treasurer, PO Box 699, St. Johns, AZ 85936.
  • Debit and credit card payments go through the county's property tax payment portal.
  • At the counter, pay at 75 West Cleveland during open hours.

An online tax account search is also on the Treasurer's site. Run your parcel through it before a sale to learn the exact amount owed.

Begin with a written petition to the Assessor. A.R.S. 42-16051 gives an owner who believes the value is too high 60 days from the mailing of the notice of valuation to file on the state form, and the postmark counts as the filing date.

The petition should name the full cash value you believe is right and support it. The law allows three approaches: income, market (citing at least one comparable property or the sale of your own), or cost, which adds building cost to land value.

Missed the Assessor deadline? The Arizona Tax Court still takes an appeal of full cash value before December 15 of the valuation year, and those papers should not go to the Assessor's office. For paperless notices, the Assessor's EagleWeb parcel database accepts the key code printed on the Annual Notice of Value.

Tax left unpaid can end in a lien sale. A county treasurer in Arizona may auction a delinquent lien to the public, and Apache County posts the liens online before an auction held each February.

Bidders compete on the interest rate or bid up a premium, and many buy either to foreclose on the lien or to earn a high rate. The Treasurer's site links to pages about certificates of purchase, redemption and foreclosure.

Own a house with unpaid tax? Get the payoff from the Treasurer, then choose among paying, redeeming or selling before the lien advances.

sections.h2: Before you close on a sale
sections.html:
Start with the balance, move to the districts, and finish with who pays what at closing. Unpaid tax can hold up a sale, so sort out the numbers early.

  • Find your parcel in the Treasurer's tax account search and verify both halves of this year's bill.
  • Request the Assessor's tax rates by district form, which shows the levies on your parcel.
  • See if your parcel is on the Treasurer's lien lists, and read the redemption page if it is.
  • Verify the owner of record. Notices go to the address on file, and the Assessor has an address change request form.

Copies from the Assessor cost $1.00 per page picked up or $1.50 per page mailed, and a data set costs $300. That can matter when a sale requires records.

On Arizona's northeastern edge, Apache County was organized in 1879 and spans 11,218 square miles, with St. Johns as its seat. Indian reservation land, including the Navajo Nation, the Fort Apache Indian Reservation and a Zuni Indian Reservation holding, makes up 68.34 percent of the area. Population fell from 71,518 in 2010 to 66,021 in 2020, and 64,445 is the 2025 estimate.

The incorporated places are the city of St. Johns and the towns of Eagar and Springerville. Other named communities are mostly census-designated places.

sections.h2: Gathering your records for a sale
sections.html:
A seller with a clear paper trail closes faster. Start with the Notice of Value, which shows how the Assessor sees the property, and the most recent tax notice, which shows what each half costs. Print the Treasurer's account page for the parcel so you have a dated record of what was paid.

Write down the date of every call and the name of the person who answered. If a figure from the Treasurer or Assessor later differs from the title company's number, those notes show where each one came from and help you settle the difference fast.

If the house sits on possessory rights land or near reservation land, call the Assessor early, since the Assessor counts improvements on possessory rights as real property. Keep any deed, lease or correspondence together so a buyer and title company see the same story.

A balance can be cleared at closing. Get the payoff from the Treasurer, hand it to the title company and have it paid out of your proceeds. If a lien has already been sold to an investor, ask the Treasurer how redemption works.

A cash sale suits an owner who would rather not wait on a lender, repairs or a listing, and the payoff steps are the same.

faqs.q: When are Apache County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Twice a year, on October 1 and March 1. The first half goes delinquent after 5:00 p.m. on November 1 and the second after 5:00 p.m. on May 1.

faqs.q: What interest rate does Apache County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: 16% a year, prorated monthly. Ask the Treasurer what your parcel owes.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Apache County assessment?
faqs.a: Sixty days from the Assessor's mailing of your notice of valuation, using a petition under A.R.S. 42-16051. After that, the Arizona Tax Court is still open before December 15 of the valuation year.

faqs.q: Where do I send my Apache County property tax payment?
faqs.a: Mail it to Apache County Treasurer, PO Box 699, St. Johns, AZ 85936 if you have no coupon, or to the Houston, Texas box on the coupon if you do. Online and in-person payment at 75 West Cleveland also work.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Apache County house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. Obtain the payoff from the Treasurer and clear it at or before closing. If an investor already bought a lien, ask the Treasurer about redemption.
